learn.title: A tree of letters
learn.body: A trie, said like try, stores words by their letters. Each step down the tree is one letter. Words that start the same share the same path, so car, cart and cat share c then a. A flag on a node says a word ends there.

learn.title: A trie node
learn.body: One child pointer per letter a to z, plus the flag. We assume lowercase words. `make` returns a zeroed node, which means NULL pointers and 0 on the usual platforms.

learn.title: Adding a word
learn.body: `*w - 'a'` turns a letter into 0 to 25. The new child comes from `make`.

learn.title: Looking up
learn.body: Follow the letters. A missing child means the word is not there. The flag tells whole words from mere prefixes.

learn.title: Is ca a word?
learn.body: The trie holds car, cart and cat.
steps: Follow c, then a. Both children exist
The walk ends on the node for a
That node's `is_word` is 0, so ca is only a prefix

learn.body: A trie finds a word in as many steps as it has letters, however many words are stored. The cost is memory: each node holds 26 pointers.

questions.prompt: What does each step down a trie represent?
questions.explanation: Following letters spells out the word.

questions.prompt: Why do car, cart and cat share nodes?
choices: They begin with the same letters
questions.explanation: Shared prefixes share the same path from the root.

questions.prompt: A node's \_\_ flag marks that a word ends there.
questions.explanation: Without the flag, a prefix like ca would look like a word.

questions.prompt: In `*w - 'a'`, what index does the letter c give?
questions.explanation: a is 0, b is 1 and c is 2.

questions.prompt: A lookup of the word dog finds no child for d at the root. What does `has` return?
questions.explanation: A missing child means no stored word starts with that letter.

questions.prompt: What is the main cost of a trie?
choices: Memory for many pointers per node
questions.explanation: Each node here holds 26 pointers, even when most are NULL.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to add a word.
steps: For each letter, find or create its child
Set is_word on the final node
questions.explanation: The flag goes on the node reached after the last letter.
